notes: The italicized let us prophesy is rightly added, but rule 103 is the governing citation rather than rule 86: προφητείαν has already spent its English on prophecy, so the supplied lexical predicate has no token left to license it. Rule 86 speaks of clause-introducers.
τῆς πίστεως → of our faith gives our to the article under rule 20's second arm, no genitive pronoun standing to take it, with the case preposition riding along under rule 21.
The second attributive τήν governs an expressed head noun, so the relativizer that is the participle's helper and the article is unrepresented (rules 23, 31).
